Adjusted using SLOOS: While the FOMC statement notes strengthening activity and strong job gains, SLOOS points to near‑term support from credit supply and demand on the business side—banks eased standards broadly (including C&I and CRE) and reported stronger C&I demand across large, middle‑market, and small firms, with expectations for improvement in business, CRE, and construction lending. Offsetting this, SLOOS shows banks expecting deterioration in household credit (auto, credit card, nonconforming jumbo) and reporting weaker demand for residential mortgages, alongside expectations for higher interest rates that align with policy tightening. Netting these, the tone remains slightly positive but cautious, with business credit strength tempered by consumer‑side fragility and tightening financial conditions.
